title: The intent-complete loop is harness-driven; rcf-lite computes questions with write-backs and never holds conversation state
context: DEFINE step 3 (spec 2026-10-01, section 1.1) requires a product owner to reach `levels.intentComplete.ok === true` without an engineer. The question is whether rcf-lite should hold a conversation state (a stored loop file, a conversation engine) or stay stateless and let the harness (Claude Code or any MCP-wired agent) drive.
decision: the loop is harness-driven; rcf-lite computes questions with write-backs and never holds conversation state. computeQuestions is a pure function of (readiness, tree, ledgers, profileText, persona); the harness runs the write-back a question carries, calls readiness again and asks the next question.
consequences: The loop is monotone (each answer removes its item), the compute is testable in isolation, and the harness can be swapped without changing rcf-lite. The cost is that the harness must run readiness and questions each turn, which is a cheap pure call.

alternativesConsidered.name: A conversation engine in rcf-lite
alternativesConsidered.summary: Hold an LLM-driven loop inside rcf-lite that elicits the PO directly.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: An LLM dependency inside rcf-lite reverses the method's shape: rcf-lite is the referee the harness consults, not an agent of its own. It also forces a model and provider choice that the harness has already made.

alternativesConsidered.name: A stored loop file
alternativesConsidered.summary: Keep a loop state file under rcf/define/ that tracks which question was asked last.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The stale state the detection model removed. A loop file would drift from the tree the moment any writer edits a ledger outside the loop, and would need its own validate pass; the four ledgers plus the profile already carry every state the loop needs.
